title: Final Parking Space: 1979 Pontiac Catalina Safari Wagon

body_markdown:
The late 1970s were glorious times for station wagon shoppers in the United States, with close to 50 distinct wagon models available through 23 different marques during the[Peak Wa](https://www.autoweek.com/car-life/classic-cars/a39372850/what-year-was-peak-wagon-in-america/)[g](https://www.autoweek.com/car-life/classic-cars/a39372850/what-year-was-peak-wagon-in-america/)[on year](https://www.autoweek.com/car-life/classic-cars/a39372850/what-year-was-peak-wagon-in-america/) of 1977. GM’s Pontiac Division was a serious wagon seller during that era, and I’ve found a rare example of Pontiac’s most affordable full-sized station wagon of 1979: this Catalina Safari in[a boneyard in Moss Landing, California](https://www.picknpull.com/locations/46/moss-landing-ca) .


Nick Pon


I was in the Monterey Bay region for the 20th Anniversary race of the 24 Hours of Lemons at[WeatherTech Raceway Laguna Seca](https://weathertechraceway.com/) , both in my capacity as the wise and fair[Judge Phil](https://www.murileemartin.com/UG/LNES12/0034-LNES12-UG.html) and as a member of two teams. One was[Team Lost in Translation](https://www.facebook.com/khv8th/) , which runs[a 1997 Mitsuoka Viewt](https://www.instagram.com/pugwonk3/) with a big-block 1.8-liter QG18DE engine from a[B15 Nissan Sentra](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9zdrQxuluzs) swapped in place of its original 1.0-liter Nissan CG10DE.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


In the runup to the Laguna Seca race, the mechanical part of the engine swap had gone well, but the new engine (which was pulled from a complete, running donor Sentra) refused to run correctly in the Viewt. With a few days to go before the green flag, something involving the Sentra’s ECU and/or engine harness and/or mysterious other factors threatened to keep the car off the track.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


I was driving to California from Denver and (as the most junkyard-knowledgeable Lost in Translation team member) volunteered to scour junkyards along my route for a replacement QG18DE brain from a 2000-2006 Sentra with a manual transmission and no starter-interlock security system. These ECUs must fail often, because I looked in dozens of such cars in Nevada and California car graveyards and found exactly *one* ECU still present in a non-[NATS](https://www.nissan.co.uk/owners/car-repair/car-owner-manual/manuals/iom/juke/0f16/e1/2024/nissan-anti-theft-system-nats-where-fitted-2.shtml) manual B15 Sentra: this one in a Pick-n-Pull near the original Tesla Factory. Yes, all those stickers on my toolbox were peeled off junkyard cars.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


As it turned out, the ECU I pulled wasn’t compatible with the harness of the original engine donor, so the team captain ended up buying *another* engine donor car and doing[a frenzied last-second swap](https://www.instagram.com/p/DeXEdeIi9LY/?xtok=MTN6anF3YmJtNTRteA%3D%3D) to get the car into the race. The good news was that all those ECU-seeking junkyard visits gave me the opportunity to shoot even more interesting vehicles than usual for such a trip. Our[Ford-obsessed Sajeev Mehta](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/sajeev-mehta/) was twisting my arm to write about this fully-loaded-yet-still-manual-equipped Thunderbird Turbo Coupe for today’s FPS, but I felt we were overdue for a GM station wagon here.


Pontiac Division, General Motors


GM downsized its full-sized models for the 1977 model year, which meant that the company’s biggest U.S.-market wagons lost nearly eight inches of wheelbase and about a half-ton of curb weight. Such iconic B-Body family haulers as the Estate Wagon, Custom Cruiser, Bonneville Safari, and Caprice Estate still scaled in at roughly two tons apiece, but they’d shed enough bulk to be prepared for[certain geopolitical events](https://www.federalreservehistory.org/essays/oil-shock-of-1978-79) then on the horizon.


Pontiac Division, General Motors


For the 1977-1980 model years, Pontiac offered three distinct sizes of station wagon for the United States market. The biggest was the B-Body Bonneville/Catalina Safari. The midsize A-platform-based Pontiac wagon was the LeMans/Grand LeMans Safari, while the Vega-derived Sunbird Sport Safari was the subcompact offering.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Pontiac began using the Catalina name as[a trim-level designation in 1950](https://oldcarbrochures.org/United%20States/Pontiac/1950_Pontiac/1950%20Pontiac%20Catalina/index.html) . For 1959, the Catalina became a separate model, serving as the entry-level big Pontiac through 1981. The Catalina generally outsold its plusher Bonneville sibling during the 1959-1981 period, but[the Bonneville name survived](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/unpredictable-life-cycle-of-pontiacs-bonneville-nameplate/) all the way through 2005.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Not only did Pontiac Safari shoppers have the choice of three sizes of wagon in 1979, but the engine selection choices for the Catalina/Bonneville Safari were also maddeningly broad. This car has the largest-displacement option under the hood: the 403-cubic-inch Oldsmobile V-8, rated at 185 horsepower and 320 pound-feet in 49-state trim.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The Olds 403[went into](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oldsmobile_V8_engine#403) everything from Buick LeSabres to Pontiac Firebirds in the late ’70s, and it proved to be useful as one of the few big-displacement GM V-8s that could squeeze past California’s emissions standards for that era.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The engine choices for this car were so confusing due to the California/49-state split that none of the three 1979 car price guides i have provide even close to the same list (I’m assuming that both the rules and GM’s responses to them changed at least once during the model year). The base engine on the 1979 Catalina was the 231-cubic-inch (3.8-liter) Buick V-6, while all Bonnevilles got V-8s that year.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


Outside of the Golden State, buyers of full-size Pontiacs in 1979 could get V-8s made by Chevrolet (305 cubic inches), Pontiac (301, 350, and 400 cubic inches), and Oldsmobile (403 cubic inches). It appears possible that the 403 was the *only* V-8 engine available in the Catalina Safari for the 1979 model year in California. For 1980, things got weirder still, when Oldsmobile diesel 350s and gas-burning Pontiac 265s became available, though the latter type couldn’t be had in a Catalina Safari for reasons I don’t have the energy to chase down.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The only transmission available in the 1979 Catalina was a three-speed automatic, which I’m sure saved a lot of aggravation on the assembly line as it prevented several weirdo buyers from ordering cars like a Bonneville Safari with Pontiac 301 power sent through a three-on-the-floor manual.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


This car appears to have been purchased with most big-ticket options beyond just the 403, pushing its out-the-door price far beyond that of the $6681 MSRP ($32,959 in 2026 dollars).


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The build tag tells us that it was assembled at Pontiac Assembly in Michigan, which was shut down a few years later.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The air conditioning alone cost 605 bucks (about 2985 of today’s bucks).


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


This car has lived a long and sometimes rough life. It appears that a black replacement fender was installed on the right side, while the left-side fender was sprayed with black paint to make the two match (this is the “I meant to do that” strategy of low-budget car body repair).


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The original steering wheel has been replaced with the airbag wheel from a late-1990s Chevrolet truck. I am assuming that the airbag actuation hardware was not swapped over with the wheel.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


The lichen growth suggests a lengthy period of inactivity before arriving at this yard.


[Murilee Martin](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/mmartin/)


This Safari could tell some interesting stories from[the Garlic Capital of the World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oldsmobile_V8_engine#403) .


Mileage 38% better than the 1976 Catalina*


*Percentage increase is lower in California.
